title: A Clock for the Lantern
premise: In 1893, Ansel Quintana — a clockmaker's apprentice hiding her identity as a woman and as the daughter of a hanged labor organizer — is summoned to repair the observatory's master clock in the mountain town of Vell. When the seasonal bridge closes, she discovers the clock's escapement chamber conceals ledgers proving the town magistrate framed her father and embezzled from the miners' fund. With the help of an unlikely found family — a retired smuggler innkeeper, a deaf astronomer's daughter who reads lips through glass, and the magistrate's own disillusioned son — Ansel must repair the clock while smuggling the evidence past three checkpoints before the spring thaw, when the magistrate plans to burn the observatory archives. The climax comes at the clock's midnight striking, when the town gathers to hear it run again and Ansel triggers the chimes to repeat thirteen times, forcing the magistrate to confess publicly; in the end, Ansel claims her name openly, keeps the clock, and chooses the family she built over the anonymity she wore.
about_author: Coral Okafor is the pen name of a former museum conservator who spent years restoring nineteenth-century instruments and now writes historical fiction about the people history overlooked. She lives between Lisbon and a small mountain town that inspired Vell, where she still winds a public clock every Sunday.

chapters.title: The Summons
chapters.summary: Ansel Quintana arrives in Vell under a forged letter of apprenticeship, summoned to repair the observatory's master clock. POV: Ansel. Beat: cautious hope shadowed by the fear of being recognized.

chapters.title: Gears Under Her Skin
chapters.summary: Ansel inspects the great clock, finding sabotage too precise to be wear. The head warden dismisses her questions. POV: Ansel. Beat: professional pride curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: First snow seals the mountain bridge for the season; Ansel realizes she cannot leave until thaw. At the Lantern Inn, innkeeper Marta Sable watches her too closely. POV: Ansel. Beat: trapped restlessness.

chapters.title: Thirteen Strokes
chapters.summary: The clock strikes thirteen during testing — a signal, not a malfunction. Old miner Ivo recognizes the trick from the strike years ago. POV: Ivo. Beat: dread awakening old grief.

chapters.title: Marta's Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Marta offers Ansel lodging in exchange for fixing the inn's regulator clock, probing gently about her past. POV: Marta. Beat: guarded kindness, a smuggler sizing up a fellow runner.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Reads Glass
chapters.summary: Ansel meets Odile, the astronomer's deaf daughter, who communicates by lip-reading through the observatory's telescope room window. They bond over mechanisms. POV: Odile. Beat: first friendship, being seen without words.

chapters.title: What the Escapement Hides
chapters.summary: Deep in the clock's case, Ansel finds a hidden compartment: ledgers recording payments from Magistrate Corven to witnesses who testified against labor organizer Tomás Quintana — her father. POV: Ansel. Beat: vertigo; her cover story collapses inward.

chapters.title: A Name She Buried
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Ansel watching her father hang, taking her brother's name and trade to survive. POV: Ansel. Beat: grief reframed as strategy.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Ivo maps the route out: the tollhouse, the garrison gate, the ferry landing — all watched by Corven's men even in winter. POV: Ivo. Beat: cold arithmetic of risk.

chapters.title: Corven's Son
chapters.summary: Elias Corven, the magistrate's son and reluctant clerk, audits the observatory and nearly catches Ansel with the ledger. He covers for her — why? POV: Elias. Beat: complicity beginning.

chapters.title: The Warden's Cut
chapters.summary: Head Warden Brannock, loyal to Corven, orders the clock's tower sealed 'for safety,' trapping the evidence inside. POV: Ansel. Beat: the walls tightening.

chapters.title: Lessons in Lip and Light
chapters.summary: Odile teaches Ansel to pass messages via lantern signals across the square; Marta joins the circle uninvited and stays. POV: Odile. Beat: found family assembling itself.

chapters.title: The Tollhouse Man
chapters.summary: Ansel scouts checkpoint one disguised as a clock-mender on call, memorizing shift changes and the guard's weakness: gambling debts. POV: Ansel. Beat: fear transmuted into craft.

chapters.title: Elias Asks Questions
chapters.summary: Elias confronts Ansel: he found his father's signature pattern in the ledgers' margins. He wants truth more than loyalty. POV: Elias. Beat: a crack in the house of power.

chapters.title: Midwinter Fair
chapters.summary: During the fair, the team rehearses the smuggling route amid crowds; a near-discovery forces Marta to reveal her old smuggling skills. POV: Marta. Beat: the crew becoming a unit.

chapters.title: Brannock's Warning
chapters.summary: Brannock tells Ansel he knows who she is — and offers to look away if she leaves the ledgers and goes. POV: Brannock. Beat: temptation of the easy exit.

chapters.title: What Justice Weighs
chapters.summary: Ansel debates with Ivo: expose Corven through courts that failed them, or outside the law entirely. POV: Ivo. Beat: moral argument at the story's hinge.

chapters.title: The Copy
chapters.summary: Odile transcribes the ledgers into braille and ciphered notes so the originals can stay hidden as bait. POV: Odile. Beat: quiet heroism, competence as love.

chapters.title: Checkpoint One Falls
chapters.summary: They settle the tollhouse guard's debts through Marta's old network; he looks elsewhere on the night they move a decoy satchel. POV: Marta. Beat: first victory, brittle with luck.

chapters.title: Corven Smells Smoke
chapters.summary: Magistrate Corven orders the observatory searched after a fire at the records office; Elias must choose what to report. POV: Elias. Beat: betrayal or conscience.

chapters.title: Sealed Tower, Open Night
chapters.summary: With the tower locked, the crew enters through the pendulum shaft in darkness; Ansel nearly falls, saved by Odile's rope-work. POV: Ansel. Beat: terror and trust entwined.

chapters.title: The Garrison Gate
chapters.summary: Checkpoint two: Elias uses his father's seal to sign the decoy through, burning his bridges behind him. POV: Elias. Beat: irrevocable defection.

chapters.title: Brother's Ghost
chapters.summary: A traveling clock-dealer recognizes Ansel's technique as Tomás Quintana's daughter's; he keeps her secret but demands she finish what her father started. POV: Ansel. Beat: inheritance accepted.

chapters.title: Ferry Frozen
chapters.summary: The river freezes early — checkpoint three, the ferry landing, becomes impassable both ways. The plan breaks. POV: Ivo. Beat: despair at the mercy of weather.

chapters.title: Corven's Offer
chapters.summary: Corven summons Ansel, reveals he has known her face for weeks, and offers pardon and passage if she surrenders the ledgers. POV: Ansel. Beat: the villain humanized, the choice sharpened.

chapters.title: Marta's Confession
chapters.summary: Marta admits she once informed on a runner to save her own skin — and lost him. She will not lose another. POV: Marta. Beat: guilt redeemed into resolve.

chapters.title: The Clock Must Run
chapters.summary: Ansel realizes the master clock's restoration ceremony will gather the whole town — the only crowd Corven cannot disperse. New plan: make the clock itself testify. POV: Ansel. Beat: audacity kindling.

chapters.title: Thirteen Again
chapters.summary: She rebuilds the striking train to strike thirteen at midnight, wired to a second escapement holding the evidence chamber open. POV: Ansel. Beat: artistry as weapon.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Inn
chapters.summary: Brannock, pressured by Corven, tips off the search — but only after warning Marta to clear the inn, choosing the town over the magistrate. POV: Brannock. Beat: divided loyalty resolved sideways.

chapters.title: The Search
chapters.summary: Soldiers tear through the observatory; Odile misdirects them with false lantern signals while the real ledgers sit inside the clock. POV: Odile. Beat: nerve stretched to snapping.

chapters.title: Elias Before His Father
chapters.summary: Corven confronts Elias with proof of his treachery; Elias answers with the miners' names his father ruined. POV: Elias. Beat: son against father, no way back.

chapters.title: Restoration Eve
chapters.summary: The town prepares for the ceremony; Ansel, exhausted, lets Marta braid her hair openly as a woman for the first time in years. POV: Ansel. Beat: identity chosen, not hidden.

chapters.title: Ceremony of Gears
chapters.summary: Corven presides over the restored clock, planning to announce new taxes; Ansel stands among the crowd, hand on the release lever hidden in her coat. POV: Ansel. Beat: held breath.

chapters.title: Thirteen Strokes at Midnight
chapters.summary: The clock strikes thirteen; the chamber opens; pages rain onto the square. Ivo reads the ledgers aloud by lantern light. POV: Ivo. Beat: catharsis — the dead man's name spoken by hundreds.

chapters.title: The Crowd Decides
chapters.summary: Corven orders arrests; the garrison, mostly miners' sons, refuses. The town, not the law, delivers judgment — Corven is confined to his house pending trial. POV: Elias. Beat: justice outside the law, imperfect but real.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Bells
chapters.summary: Days later: trials promised, Brannock resigns, the bridge reopens early. Ansel could leave free and anonymous. POV: Ansel. Beat: the exit door standing open.

chapters.title: Her Father's Bench
chapters.summary: Ansel visits her father's grave above the tree line with Ivo and Odile, leaving a small brass escapement on the stone. POV: Ansel. Beat: grief finally given ritual.

chapters.title: The Apprentice's Papers
chapters.summary: Ansel signs her true name — Anselma Quintana — to the guild papers restoring the clock, witnessed by Marta, Odile, Ivo, and Elias. POV: Ansel. Beat: identity claimed in ink.

chapters.title: Spring Thaw
chapters.summary: The bridge opens fully; travelers ask about the clock that struck thirteen. The found family remains: Marta keeps the inn, Odile the observatory, Elias the reform petitions. POV: ensemble. Beat: warmth after long winter.

chapters.title: A Clock for the Lantern
chapters.summary: Years later, Ansel fits a small lantern-lit dial to the tower so the time can be read across the square at night — a gift to the town that saw her. Final line echoes the opening summons, now answered. POV: Ansel. Beat: belonging, hard-won and kept.
